summary: Verified a bounded deterministic delivery-DAG canary using existing CURRENT owners. Producer and QA-precompile start together; independent checks wait only for their real prerequisites; a slow ASYNC_AFTER_CANDIDATE visual verifier does not block a reversible usable candidate or the promotion fan-in; a real promotion blocker still prevents promotion when failed. Compared with an equivalent serial schedule, the fixture reduces promotion-ready critical path from 22s to 16s and all-QA wall clock from 32s to 22s without changing CURRENT or promotion authority.
tests: PASS_TIMING: candidate usable=12s, DAG promotion-ready=16s, DAG all-QA=22s, serial promotion-ready=22s, serial all-QA=32s.
PASS_ADVISORY: visual_advisory PENDING does not block candidate visibility or promotion fan-in.
PASS_BLOCKER: security_gate FAIL preserves candidate usability but makes promotionReady=false.
PASS_AUTHORITY: no CURRENT, Human Accepted, Served or promotion authority changed.
recommendation: Use DAG granularity at dependency/owner/blocking-scope boundaries: producer, QA-precompile, independent verifier classes and judge. Fill spare capacity with grounded verifier/critic slices rather than duplicate producers; fan-in waits only on explicit blockers.
unresolved: This fixture proves dependency/timing semantics, not real distributed scheduler parallelism. A separate runtime canary is needed only if actual wall-clock concurrency itself must be promoted from simulated semantics to runtime evidence.
